copy.normal: Hercul sees your CNS load running {cns.acwr|1dp}× your four-week average. That is the point where progress starts costing more than it returns — take a deload week.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.acwr|1dp}× your four-week average and no deload in sight. You are not being hard, you are being slow. Take the week.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your CNS is running high today — readiness {cns.readiness|pct}%. Good day for isolations. Push the heavy compounds to your next session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.readiness|pct}% readiness. Whatever heroic compound you had planned today, it is going to be a bad rep at a weight you already own. Do isolations.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you fully recovered — readiness {cns.readiness|pct}%. This is the day to go after a top set.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {cns.readiness|pct}% readiness. No excuses available today. Go and be heavy.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets this week. If your shoulders complain on bench, that ratio is the first place to look.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} sets of chest and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} of rear delts. Then you wonder why your shoulders hurt on bench. That is not bad luck, that is arithmetic.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.pushPct|int}% of your volume going to pushing. Pulling builds the shoulders that let you keep pushing — even it up over the next few weeks.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.pushPct|int}% push. You are building the half of your body you can see in the mirror and quietly skipping the half that holds it together.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Quads|int} quad sets against {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} for chest this week. Legs carry everything else — give them a real session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Quads|int} sets of quads. Your upper body is thriving and your legs have been quietly retired. Hercul is not angry, just disappointed.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets this week — past the point most people can recover from. More is not the missing ingredient here.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {volume.weeklySets:Chest|int} chest sets. You are not training chest any more, you are just visiting it repeatedly.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you hitting {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target this week across {session.sessionsThisWeek|int} sessions. You are training hard enough to deserve the recovery — one more solid portion a day covers it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.sessionsThisWeek|int} sessions this week and {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target. You are paying for the gym and refusing to collect.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you averaging {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target while cutting. The target is the plan — either eat to it or move it deliberately.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target on a cut. That is not a cut, that is maintenance with extra paperwork.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your calorie target while you are trying to gain. Muscle is built from surplus, not from good intentions.
copy.honest: Hercul sees you trying to grow on {nutrition.kcalPct7d|pct}% of your target. You cannot build a house and skip the bricks.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.daysLogged7d|int} days logged out of seven. He is not going to draw conclusions from that — and neither should you.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.daysLogged7d|int} days logged this week. Hard to fix a diet nobody is willing to look at.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% of your protein target, six days logged. This is the boring part that actually works. Keep it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {nutrition.proteinPct7d|pct}% protein and a full week logged. Fine. Hercul has nothing to complain about. Do not let it go to your head.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your weight has moved {body.weightDeltaKg:21|abs} kg in three weeks while you are cutting. Nothing is broken — the intake just is not where you think it is. Re-weigh portions for a week or take another 200 kcal off.
copy.honest: Hercul sees three weeks of cutting and {body.weightDeltaKg:21|abs} kg to show for it. Something is not making it into the log. Hercul is not angry, just disappointed.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your bodyweight flat over three weeks on a gaining phase. Add 200 kcal and hold it for a fortnight before judging it.
copy.honest: Hercul sees three weeks of "bulking" and no bulk. You are eating like someone who is scared of the scale.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg down in two weeks. That is faster than muscle survives — ease the deficit unless there is a reason for the hurry.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {body.weightDeltaKg:14|abs} kg gone in a fortnight. Some of that was muscle you spent a year earning. Slow down.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {exercise.lastPerformedDays:barbell-back-squat|int} days since your last squat, while everything else is on schedule. Put it back at the front of a session.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {exercise.lastPerformedDays:barbell-back-squat|int} days since you squatted. Everything else is going great. Funny, that.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {session.daysSinceLastWorkout|int} days since your last session. Do not try to make it up — just do a normal workout today.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.daysSinceLastWorkout|int} days. The plan does not care why. Go and do a session, an ordinary one, today.

copy.normal: Hercul sees {session.sessionsPerWeek4w|1dp} sessions a week for a month straight. That consistency is worth more than any single programme.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {session.sessionsPerWeek4w|1dp} sessions a week for four weeks. Hercul has checked twice and can find nothing wrong. Unsettling.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you squatting regularly at {profile.heightCm|int} cm. Longer femurs force more forward lean to keep the bar over midfoot, so a low-bar position or a heeled shoe usually buys back the depth you are fighting for. Worth a three-week trial.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm grinding high-bar squats. Your femurs are never going to make that look like the video. Go low-bar or put your heels up — it is leverage, not character.

copy.normal: Hercul sees your sumo deadlift sitting at {exercise.e1rmRatio:sumo-deadlift:barbell-back-squat|1dp}× your back squat. At {profile.heightCm|int} cm that is largely anatomy — a wide stance asks a lot of long femurs. Conventional often suits your build better; run it for a block and compare.
copy.honest: Hercul sees your sumo barely clearing your squat at {exercise.e1rmRatio:sumo-deadlift:barbell-back-squat|1dp}×. Some of that is being {profile.heightCm|int} cm and pulling the stance that punishes it. Pick conventional, commit to a block, then argue.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you benching often at {profile.heightCm|int} cm on {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets a week. Long arms mean a longer bar path and more triceps off the chest, and the shoulder spends longer at end range — direct rear delt and rotator work is part of the lift, not an extra.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm of leverage against you on bench and {volume.weeklySets:Rear Delts|int} rear delt sets defending the joint. Long arms make that press a shoulder-health problem before it is a chest problem. Fix the back of the shoulder.

copy.normal: Hercul sees you pulling conventional at {profile.heightCm|int} cm — a shorter build usually keeps the bar close and the back angle friendly here. Worth trying a heavier top set before assuming sumo is the answer.
copy.honest: Hercul sees {profile.heightCm|int} cm pulling conventional. That is the stance your build is actually good at. Stop reading about sumo and add weight.
